claim: Let \(n\ge 2\) and let a coherent system with IID continuous component lifetimes have signature \(\mathbf s=(s_1,\ldots,s_i,0,\ldots,0)\) with \(1\le i\le n-1\). If each component has the exponentiated-Weibull CDF \(G(x)=(1-e^{-(x/\lambda)^\beta})^\alpha\), where \(\alpha,\beta,\lambda>0\), and \(T_{n,n}(t)=Y_{n:n}-t\mid T^{(n)}<t<Y_{n:n}\), then its cumulative residual extropy satisfies \(\xi J(T_{n,n}(t))\sim-\frac{\lambda^\beta}{4\beta}t^{1-\beta}\) as \(t\to\infty\). Consequently the CRJ tends to \(0\) for \(\beta>1\), to \(-\lambda/4\) for \(\beta=1\), and to \(-\infty\) for \(0<\beta<1\). The leading term is independent of the exponentiation parameter \(\alpha\), the system size \(n\), and the signature within the stated class.

correctness.rationale: Under the IID continuous signature model, the system failure rank is independent of ordered lifetime values. Conditioning on system failure before \(t\) while the maximum survives past \(t\) makes the number of survivors asymptotically one because the component tail \(q_t\) tends to zero. The conditional residual maximum therefore has survival \(Q_t(y)=S(t+y)/S(t)\) up to a uniform multiplicative factor \(1+O(q_t)\). The squared-survival integral reduces to \(S(t)^{-2}\) times the tail integral of \(S^2\). The EW tail is uniformly \(\alpha\exp(-(x/\lambda)^\beta)(1+o(1))\) for \(x\ge t\), and the incomplete-gamma endpoint asymptotic gives \(\lambda^\beta t^{1-\beta}/(2\beta)\) for that integral ratio. Multiplication by \(-1/2\) yields the stated coefficient. All quantifiers and \(\beta\) regimes were checked analytically; no finite computation is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The anchor paper proves only a fixed-\(y\) limit and evaluates its exponentiated-Weibull example in the \(\beta>1\) case (specifically \(\beta=1.5\)), obtaining convergence of CRJ to zero. The present statement gives the first-order CRJ asymptotic for every \(\beta>0\), including the critical constant and divergent regime, and proves that system architecture and the exponentiation parameter disappear from the leading term. Focused published-database and literature searches found no statement implying this full claim. Standard Weibull excess scaling is treated as background rather than as novel.
residual_risks: An equivalent short asymptotic may exist in older reliability or extreme-value literature under different terminology and may not be indexed by CRJ/extropy keywords.

value.rationale: The recent source uses CRJ specifically to quantify uncertainty of components that remain alive after coherent-system failure and treats an exponentiated-Weibull example only in a \(\beta>1\) regime where the limit is zero. A sharp first-order rate makes that vanishing quantitative, while the \(\beta=1\) and \(\beta<1\) regimes show that the qualitative behavior changes from vanishing uncertainty to a nonzero plateau and then unbounded residual uncertainty. The leading-order cancellation of \(\alpha\) and the system signature identifies which model features matter asymptotically, making the result structurally informative rather than a routine parameter substitution.
